newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam says ADB hopes to lend $300-350 mln a year.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam says ADB hopes to lend $300-350 mln a year.

text.p: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) is hoping to grant $300-350 million in loans and $9-10 million in technical assistance to Vietnam annually, official media reports said on Tuesday.

ADB officials in Hanoi were not available to confirm the reports, which followed a meeting between Nihal Amerasinghe, Deputy Director of the Bank's Programme Department (West) of the ADB, and Deputy Prime Minister Phan Van Khai.
Vietnam's central bank said earlier this year the ADB, one of the country's chief donors, had agreed to grant loans worth more than $1.5 billion over the next four years.
Vietnam is the largest recipient of the ADB's zero-interest concessional loans.
The Vietnam News Agency said that since resuming assistance to that country in 1993, the ADB has approved 13 loans totalling $937 million, of which $120 million was disbursed in 1995-96.
"The ADB will continue to provide Vietnam with $422 million for seven projects for next year," the agency quoted Amerasinghe as saying.
The ADB is planning to open a representative office in Hanoi next month, its first in a country in transition from a centrally planned economy to a market economy.
